column1: # Known refusals: our open gaps, each one an OPEN BUG with a todo behind it.
# READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A ROW. A row here is not an accepted difference and it is not permission
# for anything. It is a refusal of something plain Metal does — which, by the owner's standing rule
# that what Metal allows we must allow, is a bug of ours — written down so the one case that holds
# it visible does not make every run red and teach everyone to stop reading the report. An accepted
# difference lives in `docs/API.md` section 10 and is justified; a degradation lives in the degrade
# catalogue and is announced. This file is neither. Nothing here is resolved by being listed.
# It is an EXPECTATION, NOT AN ALLOWLIST, and `conformance replay` holds it to that in both
# directions:
#   - a refusal that is not listed here fails the run: a new gap appeared;
#   - a row listed here that is NOT refused any more ALSO fails the run, saying the gap looks
#     fixed and the row must go.
# That second direction is the whole point. Closing a gap forces the ledger edit, so a row cannot
# outlive the bug it stands for and this file cannot rot into a silencer. It also means a row is
# checked by execution rather than by discipline, which is the standard the rest of the suite is
# held to.
# The ledger changes the exit status and nothing else. The report still prints each of these as a
# `Refused` row, with our error, with Metal's own words where its API validation refuses the call
# too, and counted in the suite's own `refused` number. Nothing is laundered.
# A row is held only against the cases a run selected, so replaying one case does not read every
# other row as fixed.
# Tab-separated. Blank lines and lines from `#` are ignored.
# case
column4: the gap it is waiting on

column1: mesh-object-draws-partial-threadgroup-6-by-4
column3: Err(Error::Bind("the bind state was refused: Unsupported(Unsupported { feature: MeshShading, needs: NotImplemented, location: None, symbol: None })"))
column4: The runtime refuses `drawMeshThreads` where the threads leave a partial object threadgroup, `Unsupported(MeshShading, NotImplemented)` out of the bind state (crates/metal2vulkan/src/bind/graphics.rs, `mesh_draw`'s `threads[i].is_multiple_of(lo[i])` test), while Metal draws it and runs the threads left over. Not a device gap: this M3 Max has mesh shading and draws every other row of the same probe. Measured on it (macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, our probe gaps/mesh/obj, one shape per process): the draw launches ceil(threads/L) object threadgroups, `threads_per_grid` is the threads asked for, and the last threadgroup on an axis runs with the threads left over as a non-uniform threadgroup exactly as `dispatchThreads:` does for compute - `threads_per_threadgroup` is min(L, threads - group*L) per axis (6 of 64 reports 6), `thread_position_in_threadgroup` and `thread_index_in_threadgroup` run over that reduced size, `simdgroups_per_threadgroup` is ceil of it over 32, and a threadgroup barrier synchronizes the threads left over alone. The cause is that Vulkan has no partial workgroup: the exact form is the one compute already uses, a region per edge dispatched at its own local size, which for a draw means several draws of several pipeline specializations and, on a grid with more than one whole threadgroup on a higher axis, a primitive order that is not Metal's; the alternative is one draw of ceil groups with the object entry reading its reduced size from its `DispatchRegion` record (`MultiRegion` 1 already carries the grid and L, and already reports ceil threadgroups and the asked-for threads), deriving the thread position and index from `lin` over that size and returning before the body past it, which is exact for everything but a threadgroup barrier and so needs a pipeline variant whose compile refuses an object function that synchronizes. Neither is built. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

column1: texture-round-trip-576
column4: Plain Metal on this M3 Max makes an 8x8 Shared 2D texture of MTLPixelFormatR10Unorm_X6 from a descriptor alone, its fresh level 0 reads zero, and replace_region/get_bytes round-trip every byte with the padding between the rows untouched (recorded over 3 runs, one outcome; Metal's own API validation let it run). The runtime refuses every creator of such a texture in memory of its own with Unsupported(NotImplemented, Format) naming the format, on the reading that Metal's textures of these formats store nothing of their own (runtime_lane::textures::padded_formats_are_made_only_over_given_memory). This measurement contradicts that reading for the device's own creator, so the refusal is wider than Metal's. Fix belongs in metal2vulkan-runtime's texture creators, the padded 10-bit format policy. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.
